newsitem.title: ARMENIA: CHESS-Russia's Ilyumzhinov reelected FIDE president.
newsitem.headline: CHESS-Russia's Ilyumzhinov reelected FIDE president.

text.p: Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, youthful millionaire leader of the Russian ethnic region of Kalmykia, won a second term as president of the International Chess Federation FIDE at its annual congress in Armenia on Tuesday.
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said he won 87 of the 138 delegates' votes during the 32nd Chess Olympiad in Yerevan.
Ilyumzhinov, 34, won the FIDE presidency last November. He quickly stirred controversy with a plan, later scrapped, to hold a world championship match in embargo-hit Baghdad.
Russia's Anatoly Karpov eventually beat Gata Kamsky of the United States for the crown in a contest staged in Elista, capital of Ilyumzhinov's tiny fiefdom on the Caspian.
Ilyumzhinov hopes to close the schism at the top of world chess by arranging a match between Karpov and Garry Kasparov, the Russian grandmaster who broke away from FIDE and set up his own body.
